prs.title: Research notes (no κ claim): E8 decoder floors are tight; extension-ring, triple and Lorentzian units lose after helpers; cold-end, dispatch and fusion-search negatives
prs.body:
**No κ claim.** These are research notes on the E8 unit geometry and on supplier and outer levers. Everything is in `research/e8-decoder-floors-and-cold14-notes/`: one `README.md` with 16 sections, plus a package per section. Each package has its scripts and logs, and most have a `verify.sh` with expected outputs. SAT results have no proof logs unless stated otherwise.

## Headline results

**Gaussian E8 is nearly closed as an E8 replacement.** The unit is E8 over ℤ[i]: 60 lines, window 4. A decoder that beats real E8 needs Theorem-C cost ≤ 42. Proven:
- every decoder costs ≥ 40, and ≥ max(40, 60 − c) for c totals (§10, §15);
- c = 15 costs exactly 60 (§13);
- c ≤ 18 is excluded (§14, §15);
- c = 19 is excluded (§16, MIP bounds).

What remains is **20 ≤ c ≤ 42**: c = 20 is partly done, and c ≥ 21 has an F2 2×2-support route.

**The other E8 replacements lose to E8.**
- Eisenstein (Witting, 40 lines) and Hurwitz E8 cost ≥ v over every decoder (§10).
- Real ADE systems other than E8, the triple family, Lorentzian I_{11,1}/I_{13,1} and K12 have higher ceilings in some cases, but lose once helper costs are counted (§1, §4, §5, §7).

**E8's own decoder floors are tight.** Theorem C equals the star floor: 72 / 63 / 64 for P120 / P111 / P112. The P111 decoder is unique, and deeper punctures, mixed ports and asymmetric sinks are all worse (§2).

**"No new kappa" construction savings cannot move κ.** κ depends only on the paid rank profile and the live stock; ADD and primitive counts enter only slack admission checks (§8).

**Supplier local-edit searches are exhausted on recent words:**
- fusions and triangle slots on the X54 words (§9);
- helper-donor cold kernels on #1319 (§11);
- an extended census on the 566 + 554 T74 word, which also explains why §11 missed those kernels (§12).

## Section index
| § | Topic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Real ADE root systems as units | only E8 viable (E6 row corrected, per #630) |
| 2 | E8 decoder floors | Theorem C = star (72/63/64); P111 unique; no cheaper variants |
| 3 | #615/#617 levers | e2 ends infeasible; owner map LP-optimal (historical) |
| 4 | E8 over ℤ[i], ℤ[ω], Hurwitz; K12 | minrank = v/w, so x = 1 under the star premise |
| 5 | Triple and Lorentzian families | higher X*, lose after a calibrated helper model |
| 6 | Dispatch and cold-end pricing (#639 lineage) | ck removal +1.08e-7 b; dim-7 factored ends positive |
| 7 | I_{11,1} / I_{13,1} punctures and helpers | no improving puncture; no 4-frame partition |
| 8 | Why "no new kappa" savings are zero | κ = f(paid profile, W) |
| 9 | Fusion and slot search on the fused X54 words | 0 gains; idle-overlay PRs noted as withdrawn |
| 10 | Extension-ring floors over all decoders | Eisenstein and Hurwitz excluded; Gaussian ≥ 40 |
| 11 | Cold-kernel census on the #1319 word | 0 gains (scope limited, see §12) |
| 12 | Supplier census on the 566 + 554 T74 word | why §11 missed them; extended families give 0 gains |
| 13 | Gaussian, 15 totals | cost exactly 60 (rank-drop; 3 flat orbits; 1,500-flat sweep) |
| 14 | Gaussian, 16 totals | cost ≥ 43 (level tables) |
| 15 | Gaussian, all c | cost ≥ max(40, 60 − c); c = 18 excluded (parity) |
| 16 | Gaussian, 19–20 totals | μ-packing theorem; c = 19 excluded; c = 20 partial |

## Open problems
- Gaussian E8 at 20 ≤ c ≤ 42.
- Supplier gains outside B-local kernels: the A stage and the parent/centre interface.

Earlier versions of this description covered only §1–§3. Related work: #630, #631, #634, #703, #738, #767, #801, #888, #1957, #2066.

**AI disclosure:** prepared by Joel Pulikkan (GamingPuzzled) with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code. Apache-2.0.

prs.title: Research: certify R420 forest cuts under the 104-bit cap
prs.body:
This **finite bit-circuit construction with exact scoped certificates and a generic Lean proof** saves **4,897 binary XORs** in PR543's R420 word: **26,916 → 22,019** overall, with compensation D **19,922 → 15,025**. Every preparation and restoration operation is charged. The unchanged native **104-bit** prefix cap passes. **No new κ is claimed.**

**Concurrent #759 by Oscar Fennell is credited.** It appeared during final validation with the same forest class and 14,921-XOR unconstrained floor. This independently corroborates that floor and adds an exact coefficient-constrained cut optimization, **113 fewer XORs** than its submitted 15,138-XOR D circuit, independent verification and a generic Lean proof. No priority for forest factoring or the floor is claimed. The package uses the distinct path `research/r420-forest-cut-budget/` to avoid colliding with #759.

The contribution has three linked parts:

- A minimum spanning tree and all **7,140 non-tree cycle inequalities** certify the **14,921** unconstrained optimum for the explicitly defined single-parent forest recipe. The particular seed-6 optimum needs **106 payload bits**; all three unchanged native column checkers reject it. It is an explicit failing calibration.
- An exact dynamic program checks **all 2^116 cut subsets of the fixed oriented tree** using **724 ancestor states**. Cutting at targets **5, 34, 39, 57, 78** attains the exact minimum D cost **15,025** in this class. The independently reimplemented recurrence agrees. Its complete positive-prefix maxima are **F=144651**, **B=9800790**, with `64 F^3 B^2 = 18606576056688220135806852422400 < 2^104`.
- Lean **4.21.0** proves generic XOR-circuit linearity/reversal, children-before-parent forest execution, and compensation for arbitrary helpers and arbitrary initial targets. Seven axiom reports contain only `propext` and `Quot.sound`; no `sorry` or extra axioms. Lean does not bind the concrete word or prove MST/DP, physical, or asymptotic claims.

Optimality is deliberately narrow. A positive scope-control test changes only `parent[32]` from 37 to 34 and obtains **15,023** D XORs with the same exact scalar prefix bound and valid 660-column/frame replay. It is outside the frozen cut family and correctly fails its cut certificate. That separate word has not received native or hosted replay. No best-known circuit or global constrained-optimality claim is made.

```sh
python3 -B research/r420-forest-cut-budget/reproduce.py
# Optional scoped formal and unchanged native checks:
python3 -B research/r420-forest-cut-budget/reproduce.py --lean /path/to/lean-4.21.0/bin/lean
python3 -B research/r420-forest-cut-budget/native.py --out /absolute/fresh/output --boost /directory/containing/boost
```

Expected primary result: `PASS_R420_TARGET_FOREST D=19922->15025 ADDs=26916->22019 saved=4897 columns=660 payload_bits=104 cut_states=724; uncut_optimum=14921 rejected_at_106_bits`.

Validation passed locally on macOS arm64 and on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.13 at `f0935b4ab2fd1e051d7508b56b44f143e23211e8`: [dedicated Linux CI run](https://github.com/anthonylei/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38683386510). The run retains its exact head, file inventory, environment, logs and native receipts.

Coverage:

- Source-pinned canonical reconstruction; all **660 arbitrary-input columns**, exact geometry and unchanged MOVE/COPY/ERASE paths; rank mass **5,112**, **420 helpers**, nine copies.
- **37 adversarial/positive tests**, including missing preparation/restoration, wrong coefficients, underpriced/nonminimal certificates, numeric-type source-binding mutations, recompressed source, paid neutral operations, and the out-of-class improvement.
- Independent literal unsigned-ADD enumeration of **620 small ancestor states / 7,904 cut assignments**, with corrupt-certificate controls; source-pin compatibility controls; credited semantic-D chronology checks on all 660 columns.
- Fresh unchanged C++17/Boost checks at **5/9/11 stages**: **900/1,380/1,620 formal columns**, all **6/18/24** bridge controls on both original and selected words. A frame-legal missing restoration fails all three endpoint checks. The uncut calibration fails the unchanged payload check.
- Lean compilation and axiom audit; isolated minimal relocated replay; original selected-record integrity; Python compilation and documentation/whitespace checks.

The original helper-only H2 syntax and literal K extractor reject target mixing. The semantic replacement proves and checks the same complete D boundary map; no predecessor checker is patched. The conditional chronological substitution bridge from woklerx #1194 and Arham Tahir #1311 is now checked for this exact word: the original-D splice is literally the original checked word, and the actual D supplies identical values and frames to its continuation. Full hosted-parent/whole-owner reconstruction, global finite invoices, maintained supplier adoption of semantic D and changed-word outer assembly remain open. The inherited uniform/compiler/common-label/mutable-basis/hosting/precision/tape/analytic assumptions remain. The dedicated Linux workflow runs reconstruction, all controls, Lean and both native modes; its checked revision and receipts are retained. No repository-wide suite or full multiplication theorem pass is claimed.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`; PR543 source: `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`. Assignment seed **6**, drawn once from OS randomness. No pinned coordination issue existed; the completed claim is local. The PR adds this research package and its dedicated CI workflow; it does not alter `upstream/` or select a new frontier.

Canonical `main` at `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` is merged without conflicts (1,817 upstream commits since the scientific base). The live selected result is now #1094 using PR589/555 R439; this certificate intentionally retains its historical R420 baseline. The old selected-record hash is checked against the byte-identical #626 checkpoint, with no expected hash changes or live-record fallback. All original data, source hashes, claim, validation and Lean files are unchanged. [REVIEW.md](https://github.com/anthonylei/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f0935b4ab2fd1e051d7508b56b44f143e23211e8/research/r420-forest-cut-budget/REVIEW.md) records the priority-revision-4 guidance, live overlap refresh, credited upstream comparison and added coverage.

Credits include eumemic's R420 construction and its cumulative community lineage; #713/#716 target pairs; #742 shared donors; #759 forests; #686/#694 helper bases and #733's stronger two-sided composition. The latter is not superseded or combined here. Tree-based parity synthesis by Vandaele, Martiel and Goubault de Brugière (arXiv:2104.00934 §3.1) is acknowledged explicitly; no literature-wide priority claim.

Prepared by **Anthony (@anthonylei)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex multi-agent assistance**, under Apache-2.0. This is not independent human peer review.

prs.title: Finite complex construction: four exact U8 B-stage shear rewrites (no new kappa)
prs.body:
This adds four exact U8 B-stage shear rewrites and a complete finite verifier. The previously submitted head omitted `verify.py` and its source pins; this update publishes them and reproduces the original result certificate byte for byte, addressing [Doug Colkitt's review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1115#issuecomment-6161594838).

For distinct registers, four fragments beginning at B indices 176, 194, 204 and 278 are replaced exactly:

```text
x += a*s; y += q*x; x -= a*s
    -> y += q*x; y += (q*a)*s
```

## Result

- B-stage operations: **1,918 → 1,914**.
- Scalar macros saved per orientation: **4**.
- Forward real-component primitive bound: **193,306 → 193,254**.
- Backward real-component primitive bound: **193,354 → 193,302**.
- Exact arbitrary input columns: **728**; paid rank profile preserved.
- Rewrite negative controls rejected: **9**.
- No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

## Complete replay and inputs

`SOURCES.json` declares the immutable input closure: the already committed `research/community-frontier942-audit/t37-replay.tar.gz` (SHA-256 `48285025105210b56a32d3d4d57a21b7591760acc709d38073e4dca339eb06fe`) and the exact hashes of its canonical word, baseline emitted programs, and baseline receipts. The canonical-word digest remains `387a2266ffe006d20042221d967f67a4b18d9bb8de1cd1e01d4031b539fa74a5`.

The primary verifier uses only the standard library, reads pinned regular archive members without extraction, and imports no construction code. It checks each local identity and both complete B-stage maps with exact rational arithmetic, regenerates both baseline programs, compares the baseline receipts, and recomputes the candidate maps and primitive invoices. Its result must match the original `RESULT.json` byte for byte.

The package test exercises normal and optimized isolated Python, relocation with only the package and declared archive, and four rejection controls: missing source pins, mutated archive bytes, a wrong member pin, and changed result bytes. These checks remain active under `-O`.

## Reproduce and validation

Python 3.10+ and the standard library:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/u8-b-cancellation-seed32/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/u8-b-cancellation-seed32/test_package.py
```

Both commands pass. Normal, optimized, and relocated results match the committed certificate exactly. The updated PR applies cleanly to main at `ae95f60feec79897b153dba6459bb3f9fd4d7b8e`, where the optimized package test also passes. `git diff --check` is clean.

The retained local emitter and independent frame/wrapper auditor were rerun on the verified candidate. Both orientations preserve the paid profile, 728 columns, and 192-bit allowance; prefix bounds are 55/72 bits and all 25 inherited controls are rejected. `VALIDATION.json` records this evidence and the exact validation-source hashes. The README includes the additional reproduction commands.

## Scope and attribution

This establishes finite B-stage equality and local admission. It does not rebuild global hosting, the complete supplier invoice, outer inequalities, all-size/compiler or realization interfaces, precision/tape or exact recovery, or analytic transfer. It claims no new kappa, practical multiplication speedup, or formal proof of the complete theorem.

Assignment seed: 32, complex-supplier track. Original base: `abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf`.

Prepared for @martinxxx9 with substantial OpenAI assistance. The complete verifier and input pins were reconstructed and published with OpenAI Codex assistance in response to the review. Retain Jonathan Capalbo (#942), Chafik Boukhalfa (#890/#741), Jeremy Kothe (#869/#870/#799), Hao Yan (#858), icekylinx, DreamingOfClouds, and the source notices' full contributor and AI-assistance attribution. New material is Apache-2.0; no independent human review is claimed.

prs.title: Research note: restoration coalescing across a recursion batch (read-free + composable-family boundary; no new kappa)
prs.body:
## Status: research note (scoped mechanism + complete cost recurrence; no new kappa)

Track **recursive-interfaces** (50-59), assignment seed **53** (OS CSPRNG). One
explicit way to eliminate boundary/restoration work with a complete cost
recurrence, a sufficient correctness condition (with the exact defect criterion
behind it), and a sharp cost boundary. Contributor:
**Navinor (Aaron Wang)**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

### What is learned

A recursion node that restores its borrowed dirty workspace after **every** child
pays `r` restoration passes. This note prices one operator-level rewrite: let the
workspace drift across the batch and replace the `r` restorations by the **one**
composed restoration `(G_r...G_1)^{-1}` at the node exit. Two independent
questions decide it, both decidable exactly:

- **Correctness (vanishing defect; read-free is sufficient, not necessary).**
  The single deferred restoration returns the same observables (final data and
  final workspace) exactly when the summed defect vanishes,
  `sum_i B_i (G_{i-1}...G_1 - I) = 0`. Read-free batches make every term vanish
  separately and are sufficient, but they are **not necessary**: nonzero readers
  can cancel (exact counterexamples:
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1199,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1203,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1205). The certificate's
  reader example shows only that one reader child *can* break deferral; a second
  case replays the exact nonzero-reader cancellation (5 restorations -> 1).
- **Cost (composable family; density is not application cost).** The rewrite
  removes passes only when the restoration operators stay cheap under
  composition: unit phases -> one phase pass, permutations -> one routing pass
  (`r -> 1`). A **heterogeneous** mix (phase + Walsh + permutation) composes to
  a dense product that *retains its cheap factorization*: applying the factors
  sequentially costs the eager sum (`16` = `16` multiplications at `N = 8`,
  verified against the exact dense product). Deferred application costs *more*
  only when no cheap factorization is retained and the dense product must be
  applied directly (`64` vs `16` multiplications at `N = 8` — a statement about
  direct dense application). Structure, not the count alone, decides.

### Reproduce

Standard library only, Python 3.10+ (verified on 3.12 and 3.13), from the repo root:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/restoration-coalescing/verify.py
```

Expected first line:

```
PASS_RESTORATION_COALESCING phase=3->1(x3) perm=3->1 hetero_dense=True reader_diverges=True reader_cancels_5to1=True hetero_mults=eager16|factorized16|dense64
```

The checker recomputes the certificate and compares every field with
`research/restoration-coalescing/CERTIFICATE.json`, failing on drift. It builds
every operator explicitly at `N = 8` over exact Gaussian rationals (no floating
point, no random tolerance, no imported supplier verifier), derives each composed
restoration from the exact dense product, and self-checks any cheap structured
application against that product on the standard basis before trusting its cost.

### Base commit and pins

- Base: `ce7ad1b6ab09452c3478723a2e96ed5ff212dc08` (current `origin/main`).
- Branch: `research/agent-13-recursive-seed53` (isolated research
  package under `research/restoration-coalescing/`; no generator, `upstream/`, or
  selected-construction file touched).
- Selected result at base unchanged: `kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000`
  (CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1094 on CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1087).
- Exact source/dependency pins and file digests: `research/restoration-coalescing/SOURCE-PINS.json`.

### Relationship to concurrent work

This is a second, independent treatment of the restoration question with a
meaningfully different method (exact operator algebra and structure detection,
standalone sub-second, versus assembly-level pricing on frozen payloads). It does
**not** claim priority on "restoration deferral" and does not reproduce others'
numbers.

- [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1012)
  (thakrarsagar, same track) prices restoration deferral of U8 helper rank/frame
  climbs at the hosted T37 assembly level and finds it mass-neutral. Different
  layer and cost unit (rank mass vs. phase/routing passes); complementary, not a
  contradiction.
- [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#974](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/974)
  (avirazza, same track) prices the same boundary classes with zero parent cost.

Where those notes give the assembly-level ceiling effect, this note gives the
operator-level preconditions (vanishing summed defect + composable family) for a
genuine
`r -> 1` pass reduction at all. Both are needed before deferral is placed in a
real supplier call.

### Scope and inherited assumptions

A restoration-elimination mechanism, its recurrence, and its exact applicability
boundary. **Not** a construction, not a new kappa, not an all-size physical
compiler, precision contract, common tape, analytic transfer, owner schedule, or
the integer-multiplication theorem. Finite checks are exact algebraic identities
and exact cost counts; they do not certify a whole E8 word or the selected
`kappa`. Neither the selected frontier nor `upstream/` changes. Inherited
all-size/compiler, hosting, precision/tape and analytic assumptions remain with
their existing constructions. No independent human or proof-assistant review is
claimed. Relevant check run: the package's own verifier (full `make verify` and
the selected cold replay are untouched by this isolated package and were not run).

prs.title: Independent verification: all eight K492 emitter controls (no new bound)
prs.body:

Add `research/k492-emitter-independent-controls/`, an independent reconstruction of all eight `emit.*` source-site controls in `PROOF-NOTE-R.md` on the historical #626/R492 fixture. This contribution changes no construction, selected result, mathematical hypothesis or multiplication bound.

Prior work: #766 covers all 14 assembly source sites and explicitly excludes the emitter slice; #724 supplies invoice/assembly accounting and already explains the conceptual R/R0 distinction. #675 covers owner-window and bridge evidence; #780 independently checks owner footprints using interval endpoints, while #727 optimizes occupancy checks with bitmasks. Neither the R/R0 distinction nor the interval technique is claimed as a new discovery here. Existing construction and supplier attributions are retained in the package README.

#819 supplies related gzip-portable native-owner binding; gzip-insensitive comparisons are not claimed as a new technique. A publication refresh screened 767 open and 383 closed PR titles/bodies plus the exact emitter-site names in current main; no equivalent eight-emitter suite was identified within that non-atomic snapshot. `OVERLAP.md` records the precise overlap boundaries and screening limits.

Scope limits: this does not recover the unavailable original 32-site scratch suite or `GlobalR/run504b`, execute the other 24 source sites, rebuild the native providers, or independently re-prove scalar/Clifford/phase identities, owner-window feasibility, invoice/assembly inequalities, all-size compilation, physical hosting, precision/tape or analytic transfer. It is finite implementation evidence, not a full multiplication-theorem proof.

This contribution adapts Brian Ross’s Krenn independent-verification and semantic-corruption methodology. The checker is a standalone implementation. Development and a separate code review and rerun were assisted by OpenAI Codex / GPT-6 Astra. New files follow the repository's Apache-2.0 license.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/k492-emitter-independent-controls/run.py --out /tmp/k492-emitter-publication-review-20261013
```

Fresh run on 2026-10-13: exit 0, `PASS_COMPLETE_EIGHT_EMITTER_SITE_SLICE` (CPython 3.13.2, 38.96 seconds).

- The full baseline `HOSTED.json` equals the retained #626 receipt exactly.
- Eight source controls: five fail at their required emitter line/exception class, two emit artifacts rejected by the independent checker, and the cosmetic-label control passes.
- Eighteen semantic corruptions are rejected after hash refresh; cosmetic-label and actual gzip-recompression positive controls pass.

- Fresh `BASELINE.json`, `RESULT.json`, `SEMANTIC-CONTROLS.json` and `INPUT-PINS.json` match the retained receipts byte-for-byte. All non-command source-control fields match. All 24 input pins also match committed blobs at the integration base.

`README.md`, `REVIEW.md` and machine-readable receipts document the contract and limitations. `PUBLICATION.md` and `evidence/PUBLICATION-NORMALIZATION.json` document replacement of personal checkout prefixes in 20 provenance fields across 12 receipts. Original source/hash values and mathematical evidence are preserved; `MANIFEST.json` identifies the publication bytes. Broad construction tests and a new cold provider rebuild were not run because the change is confined to this independent finite-check package.

prs.title: Tooling: exact frame solver and delivery-rewrite search for gauge44/k8 local words (no new κ)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `research/exact-frame-toolkit/`: the search and admission tools behind the companion construction PR #1195 (two
source-holder fusions on #1148's joint-entrance k8 word). **No new κ.** No selected record, upstream file or existing package is modified.

**Revision 2 (2026-10-14)** answers the review continuation point
([comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1186#issuecomment-6161623948)). It also fixes two harness
screen gaps. Details are in the README sections *What is certified* and *Revision 2*.

**Revision 3 (2026-10-14)** makes the toolkit run on Windows, answering woklerx's independent audit
([comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1186#issuecomment-6169503528)). The platform-dependent
pieces move into `compat.py`, `portability.py` checks the Windows code paths on any OS, and the toolkit refuses `-O`.
`frames.py` is unchanged. Results are in `PORTABILITY.json` and the README section *Revision 3*.

- **Frame solver** (`frames.py`). Each solve carries two per-instance certificates:
  - exact optimality for the floored integer surrogate weights `floor(2^40 · lo_r(b))`;
  - with `interval=True`, a rigorous rational interval for the true per-call moment at b over every assignment of the frame
    model.

  The interval's lower end is a chain-dual (or exact-elimination) bound with outward-floored weights on a 2^-224 grid, plus
  a λ·rank shift that telescopes along every register chain. Its upper end is the engines' upper bound of the returned
  assignment. L/U domain propagation, chain dual decomposition and exact elimination; models monotone chains, target caps,
  cut equality, mutable early tails, and `audit_local`'s helper cones as caps (`model.py`).
- **Pricing harness** (`harness.py`): build_tri-style edits (B deletes/inserts, early tails, FULL prepends). Screens, in order:
  1. the auditor's static program rules;
  2. the B+tail+prepend map mod p;
  3. an exact check that the derived compensation is unchanged;
  4. frames.

  Every negative delta and every returned word is re-checked by the unchanged `audit_local.py`. With `interval=True` it also
  returns the true realized delta (`realized_delta_units`) and a bound on any possible true gain (`max_gain_units`).
- **Searches**: read-fusion candidates (`fusion.py`), joint triangle-hybrid candidates (`joint.py`), and the multiprocess
  fusion + enlarged-reader repair sweep (`repair.py --interval`, `sites.py`).
- **Composition**: split a slot recipe and price its instances (`slots.py`); compose slots with fusions (`compose.py`); put a
  newer word's entrances and ends onto a scalar program and re-solve (`transplant.py`).
- **Exact κ** (`kappa.py`): the certified moment root and the retained 47-constraint outer assembly with PR589, for any T.
- **Admission drivers** that reuse unchanged package engines: PR635 native chain (`native.py`), PLAN/SPEC rebinding with
  unchanged widths (`rebind.py`), `unpin.py` between discovery and `freeze_spec.py`, the T16 discovery run
  (`t16_discover.py`), and per-site negative controls (`controls.py`).

Pure Python 3.11+ with NumPy, on Linux, macOS and Windows; no C++, Boost, LP/MILP solver or network. Do not run it with
`-O`: its asserts are checks, so it refuses to start.

## Check

```sh
python -B research/exact-frame-toolkit/selftest.py      # about 50 s here (Python 3.12 and 3.14); --quick about 25 s
python -B research/exact-frame-toolkit/portability.py   # the Windows code paths on any OS, then the selftest
```

On a GitHub Actions Windows runner (Windows Server 2025, Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.5.4) the full selftest and the portability check pass, `-O` is refused, and the
spawn-mode `repair.py --interval` sweep of the pre-slot word matches the macOS sweep in all 2,405 records
([run](https://github.com/mdumitrean/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38621712253)).

It uses only files on main:
- the retained #1042/#1094 replay archives;
- #1094's `REPLAY.json`;
- #942's checkpoint and the `ASSEMBLY.json` it names.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `kappa.py` on #1094's (T16) and #942's (T37) complex profiles | the selected and checkpoint κ, exactly |
| surrogate frame optimum of the seven-slot k8 word `c2b29430` | its published profile (integer certificate) |
| true-moment interval of that word at b | published frames within 1.48e-11 units of the minimum over the frame model; the surrogate alone bounds this only by 1512 units |
| control: deliberately worse assignment | interval width = its exact true excess (6763.29 units) |
| control: exact dual with multipliers of magnitude 2^62–2^90, then a NaN | still a lower bound in Python integers; NaN rejected |
| control: port written at the end of B, undone in the first early tail | passes the B+tail screen; harness `compensation-changed`; `audit_local` endpoint failure |
| #1018's seven slots on the pre-slot word `db2c7cfb` | −1788 surrogate units each, −12516 together; certified true gains of −1784.83 each, −12493.80 together |
| source-holder fusion + full read-set exchange at slot sites X=439, X=444 | −3957 each |
| five slots + both fusions | −16854; `audit_local` PASS; unchanged interfaces; κ 0.001672756914849856 on #1094's owners |

`exchange.py` also regenerates the published SW4 word from the promoted word, as a self-check of the exchange family.

## Usage

The README covers the modules, a workflow (price → search → compose/transplant → admit), and the model and pitfalls, e.g.:
- the unpin step that `freeze_spec.py` needs after a word change;
- `emit_allcold.py` reading `SPEC.data.plan_sha256` directly;
- `evidence/local` in the gauge44 T16 packages being historical #645 files.

On the pre-slot k8 word, `repair.py --workers 6` sweeps 2,405 fusions in about 6 minutes; the only negative surrogate
deltas are the two sites above. With `--interval` (about 8 minutes), no other priced candidate can gain more than 3.3e-11
units at b. `REVISION2-REGRESSION.json` compares both revisions on this sweep.

## Scope

Search output is nomination data. A construction exists only after the unchanged package chain admits it, as in #1195.

The certificates are per-instance statements at the stated endpoint b. Neither the global recursive moment root nor κ is
inferred from cost units: both are recomputed by `kappa.py` and the package chains.

The inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape,
analytic-transfer and bit H1–H5 assumptions remain. This is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

## Attribution

Imports or ports, unchanged in substance, the following (credits in `NOTICE.md`):
- chafreaky's frame-domain model and engines;
- the k492/multicold moment and outer engines;
- icekylinx's #645 `audit_local.py`;
- Tekalign's independent recount;
- BRoute's SW4 exchange;
- NewBArch's #869 `build_tri` semantics;
- Rohan Arun's #987 slot search and the #1018 recipe (Jeremy Kothe, MineB);
- PR635's native chain;
- Hao Yan's #858 T16 package.

Revision 2 follows the maintainer's review (Mister-Meeseeks). Revision 3 follows woklerx's independent audit.

Prepared by Marius-Paul Dumitrean with substantial AI assistance (Anthropic Claude, via Claude Code). Apache-2.0.

prs.title: Conditional κ = 0.001675658002271934: two source-holder fusions on #1148's joint-entrance k8 word
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This proposes the conditional finite witness **κ = 0.001675658002271934**, **+9.705×10⁻⁸ (0.00579%) over #1148's
joint-entrance witness 0.001675560947524449**. It is also above that word's fixed-family all-replica grid ceiling,
0.001675568675201533, which this crosses by changing the local word. That ceiling is the value #1169 attains with T37
packing, the highest open claim when this was submitted.

**Depends on #1148.** The branch starts from #1148's current head `e7d0d016` and reuses its joint-entrance word, frozen T16 owners,
`k8-eight-ends-t16` parent and `run_global.py` unchanged. Until #1148 merges, this PR also shows #1148's commits; the new
content is only `research/k8-source-holder-fusions/`.

Two of the k8 word's seven triangle-hybrid slots (#987/#1018, sites X=439 and X=444) use a two-donation form. Each is
replaced by:
- the slot's own source-holder donation (holder 10, resp. 34), with its FULL-cleanup restore;
- the **full read-set exchange** of the slot's copy pair (584, 439), resp. (590, 444), in place of the second-holder
  donation (74, resp. 98) and its early tail.

The other five slots and every entrance and end frame are unchanged, as are helper widths, rank mass and #1148's owners.
All A, B and tail frames are refitted exactly. The local paid profile changes from `{1:2364,2:498,3:412,4:130,5:82,8:8}` to
`{1:2358,2:504,3:408,4:134,5:80,8:8}`, exactly `{1:−3,2:+3,3:−2,4:+2,5:−1}` per site. The idle profile
`{1:360,24:1,48:4918}` and the 69,120 whole-helper roles in 144 calls are reused verbatim.

Start review at `research/k8-source-holder-fusions/README.md`, `PROOF.md`, `CLAIM.json` and `verify.py`.

## Validation

The complete package wrapper passed on macOS (Python 3.14, NumPy/SymPy/SciPy, **no C++ or Boost needed**). It ran cold,
rebuilding #1148's parent geometry and the native chain:
- **Parent:** #1148's `k8-eight-ends-t16` replay rebuilt from the seven-slot base and checked against all 16 parent pins.
- **Build:** the word built from #1148's word by a standard-library literal patch, with every removed element checked.
- **Local audit:** #645's independent `audit_local.py`, i.e. exact forward and dual replay of all 704 columns, frames,
  entrances and cones.
- **Controls:** **10/10 fusion negative controls rejected**; at each site: dropped restore, dropped donation, flipped
  donation sign, kept fused read, and dropped donation and restore.
- **Native:** fresh PR635 native local chain, five stages including all phase edges, with semantic identities equal to the
  rebound PLAN.
- **Strict T16 admission:** #1148's unchanged `run_global.py`. **69 admission, 12 bit-supplier, 15 controller and six
  independent T16 controls**, both exact moment engines and all **47 strict outer inequalities**.
- **Final line:** `PASS_K8_SOURCE_HOLDER_FUSIONS_COMPLETE_ADMISSION 0.001675658002271934`.

`PLAN.json.gz` is #1148's PLAN with only the word-dependent fields rebound: provider hashes, semantic identities, program
hashes and the paid profile. `SPEC.json` was re-derived by the engines' discovery → freeze protocol before the strict run.

```sh
python -B research/k8-source-holder-fusions/verify.py --base "$BASE" --work /absolute/new/output-directory
```

`BASE` is the R480 k8 + seven-slot word pinned in `research/k8-eight-ends/RECIPE.json`. `--parent-from` and
`--native-from` reuse completed replays.

The same two-site change was also strictly admitted on earlier hosts, recorded in `SEARCH.json` and not separate claims:
- 0.001672756914849856 on #1094's T16 owners;
- 0.001674194854569677 on #1129's T37 owners;
- 0.001675218651386511 on #1148's three-demotion word.

## Search and attribution

The sites come from an exhaustive exact sweep of read fusions with enlarged-reader repairs:
- on the pre-slot k8 word, 2,405 fusions, with exactly these two gains;
- on the seven-slot word, 2,217 fusions, with none.

The tools are in the companion tooling PR #1186 and are not needed for verification.

The change is width-neutral, so it also applies to #1169's T37 owners for the same joint-entrance word (idle
`{1:834,48:11374}`). There it is priced exactly at **0.001675665730846312**; that is not strictly replayed here and not
claimed. #1152's word was not rebuilt. Fresh open PRs were checked for overlap before
submission; none uses this exchange variant at these sites.

Full credit is in `NOTICE.md`.

prs.title: Research audit: X2 acceptance boundary for the selected owner map (no new kappa)
prs.body:
**Adversarial audit of one selected supplier obligation; no new κ.** Navinor, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

Task selection: `adversarial-audit` track via `scripts/choose_research_task.py` (OS-random nonce `ca8debca8488dd850dd6c0afb7398632`), card `supplier-boundary-audit` (scope key `dcdb0fa8e49b08a958d0`), refined to one named condition. Base commit `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; audited source head `0fc329d0bec93ca7cd288eaea1295172e8789810` (the selected owner map, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094).

## Question and answer

The card asks: does one selected supplier obligation follow from its actual source-bound checks?

**Obligation X2:** pending axes of distinct idle children of one physical family are disjoint, so a family's hosts on different children never share a cell (stated and checked in Josie Elliston's owner audit, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1091).

**Answer: no.** X2's acceptance does not follow from the selected record's `reproduce` command. It is enforced exactly once, at batch1099 review time, by `research/community-batch1099-audit/check_frontier1094.py` (pinned in the record's `proof_supplements`). Neither `make frontier1094-verify` (stages `historical-source`, `baseline1042-cold`/reuse, `rare-pattern-exchanges`) nor `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` (record and hash validation only, no subprocess execution) nor the `community-batch1099.yml` CI job (which runs `research/t16-owner-audit-seed67/verify.py --fetch` for its pinned claim list, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1022 through https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1087, excluding the selected supplier) executes that composition. The frozen verifier chain the replay does run (`upstream1087.tar.gz`, Hao Yan's https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/858 lineage) keys hosted cells per `(owner, child, port)` in `t16/indep16.py` and asserts only `len(pending) == rank` per child in `code/audit_allcold.py`; cross-child cell sharing is outside its rule set.

## Minimal adversarial instance

One integer in the pinned `DATA-PHASES.json` pending axes: child 1's axis 131072 at port 0 replaced by 13, already pending for child 0 (children 0 and 1 are distinct idle children of the same physical family place). Exactly one differing integer; every rank, window, role count, width and profile aggregate is preserved.

- `geometry()` rejects it: `X2: children [0, 1, 14] share axes at port 0`.
- With only the X2 check suppressed, `geometry()` returns an identical geometry object and the complete R1–R7/X1 rule set accepts the fixture. The X2 rule is the only rule that reads pending axes.
- Concrete damage: roles at time 3 and time 6 (both helper 476, owner replica 0, family 224, port 0, offset 0, width 8) resolve the same pending axis 13 of family 224 — one physical cell written twice — while every role-level rule accepts both.
- A second mutation (one axis duplicated inside a single child's list) is rejected at X2 as well. Both are failure controls with single-locus, rank-preservation and null-mutation guards.

The existing rejection batteries contain no X2-directed mutant: the owner audit's 11 controls and the frozen chain's 6 independent-t16 controls. This PR supplies the first two, answering the card's method ("construct one semantically invalid but superficially well-formed fixture and test rejection").

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_PR1094_X2_ACCEPTANCE_BOUNDARY_AUDIT`. Fresh run on Python 3.13 (Windows) in this session returned that status with both mutants rejected at X2. Deterministic record and exact input pins in `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/RESULT.json`. The repo suite `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` (with `PYTHONUTF8=1`) runs 20 tests with 5 errors and 1 skip — identical with this change stashed. The 5 errors are pre-existing environmental failures in `test_research_onboarding.PackageTests` on this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf=true` breaks the temp-fixture scaffold commit comparison); they do not involve this package.

## Files changed (new package only; `upstream/`, frozen pins and selected record unchanged)

- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/README.md` — task card, trace table, evidence, open next questions.
- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/verify.py` — stdlib-only harness (positive control, M1/M2 mutants, cell-collision witness, blindness measurement, control inventory, enforcement trace).
- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/RESULT.json` — deterministic record with source pins.
- `research/owner-x2-acceptance-boundary/TASK.json`, `VERIFY.json`, `SOURCES.json` — scope metadata and replay manifest.

## Remaining obligations (not claimed)

- The full `make frontier1094-verify` cold replay with the mutated phases was not run (needs the published frontier1042 baseline artifacts and cold replay time); frozen-chain acceptance of the mutant is code-trace evidence, not execution.
- No claim other than the selected inputs was re-audited; the historical owner-boundary-audit package was used as a method example only.
- This is a checker-coverage audit of one named obligation: not a construction, not a supplier change, not a κ claim, and not a proof of hosting soundness (X2 itself is enumerated on the pinned phases, not proved universally).

prs.title: Scoped negative result: no further helper-donor kernels or exact read re-timings on the #1297/#1305/#1324 words (no new kappa)
prs.body:
## Summary

Scoped negative result, **no new κ**. **Revision 2 (`9e944899`)** adds a rigorous true-moment bound and narrows the optimality wording, in answer to the review continuation point; details are below. **Revision 3 (`c9da5f27`)** follows #1186's portable revision 3 (`c37dfb07`), so `regenerate.py` keeps working if #1186 merges as is; the evidence is unchanged.

The census runs on #1297's two local words. #1305, #1324 and #1319's T74 exact fill use the same Git blobs. #1305 and #1324 were later withdrawn by their author, because their idle overlays move axes across Z4 families. Kernels in richer families were later found on these words: #1625 (pivot 566) and #1672 (pivot 554). Both lie outside the two families searched here.

On those words, two kernel families give **no further gain** over **all 306 helper pivots read before their first B write**, where #1297 searched four:
- #1274/#1297's two-shock helper-donor kernels, with both restoration rules;
- exact re-timing of early reads.

Every neutral candidate is surrogate-optimal with a certificate, and none can lower the per-call moment at b by more than **1e-6 cost units** (rigorous). #1305's idle overlay is the exact optimum of the donor-star class its own verifier admits; that is now a statement about a withdrawn class.

Package: `research/frontier1305-kernel-census/`. Claim and results: [discussion #1314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1314).

## Starting point, validated locally (before the withdrawals)

- **#1324 @ `43c19465`:** a fresh checkout ran `verify.py`, including fresh native replays of both words and strict admission. Result: `PASS_GLOBAL_MIXED_X54_IDLE_EXCHANGES_NATIVE_AND_STRICT_ADMISSION 0.001677380107853623` (156 s, no Boost).
- **#1305 @ `a96a5d95`:** the same run gives `... 0.001677162029073474` (127 s).
- The #1186 `kappa.kappa(H, 37)` pricer reproduces both κ values, and #1297's, exactly from their profiles.

## Results (identical on both words)

Pricing uses #1186's harness, pinned at revision 3 (`c37dfb07`; its pricing code is revision 2's, `3855fd41`):
- the auditor's static rules;
- an exact program-map screen;
- an unchanged derived compensation;
- recomputed cone caps, tail-mutable frames and cut equality;
- the surrogate optimum certified by integer duality;
- `audit_local` on every negative delta;
- a true-moment interval certificate for every priced candidate.

| Family | Candidates | Neutral (Δ = 0) | Frame-infeasible | Inexact | Gains |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| #1297 relation rule, restore at end of early cleanup | 61 (25 pivots) | 32 | 8 | 21 | **0** |
| Same relation, restore just before the pivot's first write (exact by construction) | 292 (43 pivots) | 52 | 240 | 0 | **0** |
| Exact early-read re-timings within the target's suffix segment (152 pivots) | 803 | 635 | 168 | 0 | **0** |

- **True-moment bound (revision 2):** this covers all 1,438 neutral candidates, both words:
  - the realized true delta is exactly 0, because the paid profile is unchanged;
  - no candidate can lower the per-call moment at b below the base word's frames by more than 1e-6 units, where one unit is 2^-40 of that moment. The exact rational bounds are about 1e-11 and are rounded up.

  Infeasible and inexact rows involve no cost. Every verdict, delta and profile equals revision 1's.
- **Positive control:** on #1297's input word, the census reproduces its 5+5 hooks for pivots 555/567, including the committed donors 620/628. Each is priced at −11,707 surrogate units (H1 −3, H3 +1), the realized kernel worth 2.616e-7 κ. Its true value is −11,707.88 units, a certified gain, and `audit_local` passes all ten.
- **Robustness:** all base-word verdicts and profiles are identical at #1324's endpoint weights.
- **Idle:** exact backtracking over every assignment in all 3,687 (replica, port) groups gives the optimum, and it equals #1305's selection. No size-4 group admits a three-receiver donor in that class. #1324's simultaneous swaps are the larger class that does reach (51,51,51,39).
- **Deletion screen:** prices the word with a pivot's early reads deleted and no compensation. The largest prices are pivots 439/444 (−67,944), 438/440 (−62,316) and ten pivots at −51,648 (≈ +1.16e-6 κ). This is reported as a screen, **not a bound**: on the control word the uncompensated deletion of 555/567 is frame-infeasible, while the kernels are feasible and gain.

## Evidence and reproduction

- `python3 -B research/frontier1305-kernel-census/verify.py`: standard library, ~30 s. It checks the input pins, replays all five censuses exactly in rational arithmetic, binds every priced record to exactly one census match, and recounts all evidence against `RESULT.json`. It also checks every candidate's true-moment bound against `RESULT.json` and runs the positive control. It rejects five failure controls: a one-byte input change, a changed early-read coefficient, a forged negative price, a priced edit absent from the census, and a forged bound. It is a **recount**: it does not rerun the frame optimization or the interval certificates. Registered: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result` under Python 3.12.13. `tests/test_research_*.py` passes (20 tests, 1 skipped).
- `regenerate.py --toolkit <PR #1186 at c37dfb07>/research/exact-frame-toolkit --out NEW` reruns pricing, re-timing and deletion; with `--idle-run` it also reruns the idle check. It first checks the toolkit's pinned `MANIFEST.json` and every file that manifest lists. Two consecutive revision-2 runs reproduced all 15 toolkit-dependent evidence files byte for byte, in about 9 minutes each on 12 workers. Against revision 1's evidence, 8 files are byte-identical and the other 7 differ only by the added bound fields.
- **Revision 3:** `regenerate.py` now pins #1186 revision 3's `MANIFEST.json`. `deletion.py` used the harness's private SIGALRM handler, which revision 3 replaced with `compat.deadline`; it now uses the toolkit's `compat.deadline` and `Timeout`. `verify.py` and `regenerate.py` now refuse to run under `-O`; before, `verify.py`'s guard was itself an `assert`, which `-O` strips, and `regenerate.py` had none. A fresh regeneration with revision 3, including the idle check, reproduced all 16 evidence files byte for byte (about 8 minutes on 12 workers). `RESULT.json` changes only in its toolkit pin.

## Limitations

- These are finite searched families on two fixed words in #1186's frame model, at the stated b. The surrogate optimum is certified and true gains are bounded by 1e-6 units; exact true-moment optimality is not claimed.
- Not covered:
  - compensations with three or more shocks;
  - window donors on helper readers;
  - cleanup-side corrections;
  - other words, owner maps or hosting.
- Nothing is admitted, so no native or strict replay of candidates was needed or run.
- The idle statement holds only inside #1305's `verify_idle_overlay.py` class.
- The pricing scripts need #1186's toolkit (open PR); `verify.py` does not.

## Open next question

Do three-shock or window-donor relations exist for the high-screen pivots, 438/440 and the ten −51,648 pivots? #1625 and #1672 have since found kernels in such richer families, at pivots 566 and 554.
- **First step:** extend `census.py`'s dictionary to windows `x += c·q … x −= c·q` on any register x, closing before the first write. Solve sparse dyadic combinations of at most three terms, then price with `price.py`.
- **Blocker:** about 2,500 distinct suffix vectors per pivot, so the search needs support-guided pruning.

Vendored inputs are unmodified Apache-2.0 copies; see `NOTICE.md` and `inputs/PINS.json`.

**Status: scoped negative result and exact interval replay. No new κ or supplier adoption.**

## Mathematical correction

Commit [`93db17f`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/93db17f) corrects the integral identity and the following positivity bound by restoring the missing factor `(1-a)`: if `S_r` denotes the displayed sum of integrals, the identity is `Q_r = (1-a) S_r`, not `Q_r = S_r`. Since `1-a > 0` on the stated domain, the corrected lower bound remains positive. All 57 exact-rational checks pass with this correction.

This adds a complete same-slot price audit for PR #1256's finite helper470 exception. Shrinking its existing width-eight slot to width seven and returning the freed rank to that slot's idle remainder changes the paid histogram by `e1 + e5 - e7 + e_(r+1) - e_r` (with the zero-remainder case handled separately). For the frozen width-64 interface, the raw moment strictly increases for every feasible old remainder `r=0..56`; the inherited per-call surcharge also rises.

At the pinned selected exponent, the registered exact-rational replay checks all 57 remainders and rebuilds the complete selected profile for actual old classes 2, 4 and 6. The full bill increases in all three cases. Omitting the returned rank gives a false favorable control. PR #1256's distinct two-slot relaxation remains favorable at all three actual classes, so this result does not subsume or refute that mechanism.

prs.title: Scoped obstruction + search: balanced ten-call four-SWAP residual, J^2 = J^3 kills the layer route (no new kappa)
prs.body:
# Balanced ten-call four-SWAP residual: the J^2 layer cannot decide it (no new kappa)

Prepared by **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

## Scope

One focused package, `research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/` (8 files; no other path touched, `upstream/` and frozen pins unchanged). Outcome: **partial** — a scoped obstruction for one route plus a scoped search failure; the balanced question itself stays open.

**Question.** In the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` rank-one-idempotent register model (paid calls `I + ([g]+1)uv^T`, `g in {a,b}`, `v^T u = 1`, free scalar `GL_4(F2)` mixing normalized by augmentation, all four registers arbitrary dirty restored), can `T = diag([S],[S],[S],[S])`, `S = aba = bab`, at exactly `r = 4` be realized by a **ten-call word with exactly five `a`-labels and five `b`-labels**?

This is the sole surviving sub-12 four-SWAP candidate after the concurrent label-saturation result in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1715 ("four swaps need ten or twelve calls; a ten-call word must use five of each label"), which states it claims "neither existence nor exclusion of that balanced case". It is also the second branch of the handoff https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18918391: "derive the `J^2`-coefficient-layer bound in `F_2[G]/J^3` (`sum E_i + sum_{i<j} E_i E_j = T - I`) to exclude `q = 10` in writing."

## Results

1. **Exact obstruction: the proposed layer bound is vacuous in this algebra.** Augmentation powers of `F2[G]` have dimensions `(5, 4, 4)`, so `J^2 = J^3` and `R/J^3` is just the sign quotient `F2[z]/(z^2)`: the pair terms `([a]+1)([b]+1)` and `([b]+1)([a]+1)` vanish. The expansion identity `prod(1+eps_i) = 1 + sum eps_i + sum_{i<j} eps_i eps_j (mod J^3 M_r)` is derived and checked on seeded random words, and the whole layer equation is machine-checked equivalent to `sum N_i = I_r` (200/200 random instances) — the first-order sign invariant already known from https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1414. There is no second augmentation layer to read a coefficient bound off, so no written exclusion of `q = 10` can come from `F_2[G]/J^3`; word order or a different quotient (natural `M_2(F2)` image, the commutator `[ab]+[ba] in J^2`) is required. This closes that route with the exact obstruction recorded rather than silently lowering the target.

2. **Bounded exact search of the balanced profile.** With `sum N_i = I_r` a justified lossless reduction, an ordered-tuple sampler over the 120 binary rank-one idempotents (seed 20261014) checks all 252 labelings per valid tuple, at `J^3` layer and then at full formal level in `M_4(F2[G])` (96-bit exact states). Recorded run (`--full`): **6,000,000 samples, 22,903 valid tuples, 5,771,556 labelings, 0 full-formal hits.** This is a scoped search failure over the sampled domain, not an impossibility theorem.

**Controls (all exact):** four direct words (3/6/9/12 calls, incl. the balanced 6a6b twelve-call word) hit their targets; four mutation controls fail; the search finds known-solvable instances at `r = 1` and `r = 2` (balanced `q = 6`, 3,254 witnesses); a strict-relaxation honesty control exhibits a layer-feasible word failing full equality; conjugation closure of the idempotent family; two hand-derived algebra pins bind the group implementation.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, Python 3.12 stdlib only (`verify.py --full` is about 6 minutes):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/verify.py --full
python3 -I -B research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/test_verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer --check-only
```

Expected: `PASS_FOUR_SWAP_BALANCED_J3_LAYER balanced_5a5b_unrealized_in_search layer_hits=5771556 no_new_kappa`, 9 tests `OK`, `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. `EXPECTED.json` pins the deterministic counts for both budgets and any mismatch fails the replay.

## Task card and overlap

Base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea` (selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`). Card `bit-new-register-model` / scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f`, priority revision 3, chooser nonce `cd67986ec4d736b6ed683332001aecde`, track `bit-mechanisms`; scope **refined** to the balanced ten-call residual (card allows "a fixed larger register count"). Full pre-computation card: `research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/TASK-CARD.md`; structured metadata in `TASK.json`/`SOURCES.json`/`VERIFY.json` (registered, `--check-only` passes).

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18919080 (08:01Z). Refined-object overlap searches (`find_overlap.py` with 'balanced ten-call', 'five of each label', 'ten-call balanced', 'augmentation layer', 'F2[G]/J3'; snapshots 07:53–07:54Z at 410 open PRs/358 discussions and 08:45–08:46Z at 430 open PRs/386 discussions, complete pagination) matched only https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1715, which excludes this case, and my own claim/package. No match is not a novelty certificate.

## Limitations and remaining obligations

Not checked: Lean or independent human proof review; selected-supplier cold replay; physical/compiler/hosting/precision/tape admission. Not covered: `q = 8` profiles, `r = 5` with a restored dirty extra, other label profiles, and unsampled valid tuples of the balanced domain. No claim that a balanced ten-call word does or does not exist. No new supplier, recursive profile or kappa; the selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

1. Order-sensitive exclusion (or construction) for the balanced (5,5) profile: natural `M_2(F2)`-image 5+5 meet (the image PR1705's census used), or a commutator-layer bound via `[ab]+[ba] in J^2`, which `R/J^3` cannot see. Blocked by the `J^2 = J^3` collapse recorded here.
2. The same balanced question at `r = 5` with one restored dirty extra (smallest falsifying instance of "workspace cheapens the tariff"); the sign-quotient reduction carries over verbatim.

## Credit

Predecessors: commdata2338 (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1414, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1491 — model, sign parity, three-SWAP finite result), Gareth Davidson (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1333 — free-scalar normalization), Cinna Davis (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1541 — arbitrary-workspace three-SWAP theorem), Aaron Wang (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1705 — four-SWAP `r = 4` bounds and 4+4 obstruction measurement), Ross Richardson (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1715 — concurrent saturation result, complementary; it makes this package's case the sole remaining four-SWAP candidate). Substantial AI assistance disclosed as required ("with help from opencode"). This contribution does not repeat any predecessor census and does not promote anything into the selected record.

prs.title: Scoped exact minimum: even order-3 targets diag([ab],...) need 2t calls through t = 4 (no new kappa)
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

In the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` rank-one-idempotent register model with free scalar
`GL_r(F2)` mixing (paid calls `I + ([g]+1)N`, `g in {a,b}`, `N = v phi` any binary
rank-one idempotent), the **even** order-3 diagonal targets
`T_t = diag([c],...,[c])`, `c = ab = (ba)^2`, at exactly `r = t` registers (all
registers arbitrary dirty inputs restored exactly) need exactly **`2t` paid
calls** for `t = 1, 2, 3, 4` (minima 2, 4, 6, 8). This is the first even-target
tuple class of the coordinate-CNOT line: since `c` is even, the sign quotient
maps the target to `I`, so the inherited invariants flip (`q` even,
`sum_i N_i = 0`) and no predecessor conclusion transfers. Cross-register
sharing does not beat the two-calls-per-target tariff through `t = 4`.

Written invariants (package README sections 2-3): L1' sign-quotient parity
(`q = 0 mod 2`); L2' free mixing forced to `U = I` with `sum_i N_i = 0`; and a
degree 1-3 free-layer system in `F_2<x,y>/(x^2,y^2)`, used only as a screening
filter. **Correction**
(https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1763#issuecomment-6172859400):
an earlier version of this paragraph called that system complete, and package
README section 3 called it necessary for any hitting word. Both claims are
withdrawn. At `r = 1` with every projector `[1]`, the word `b a b a` is an
exact target word (`(ba)^2 = ab = c`) with `sum_ba = 1`, so the condition
`sum_ba = 0` fails on a genuine target word. The corrected scope (package
README section 3): up to degree 3 the kernel of `F -> F_2[G]` is spanned by
`R = xyx + yxy + x + y` alone, the second claimed kernel correction
`Z = z + z^2 + z^3` having degrees up to 6 with a degree at most 3 truncation
outside the kernel, so the matched system is a necessary condition only for
words of length at most 3. The system remains a screening filter
(`layer_ok_even_target`): it holds on the attaining words used here and
rejects the wrong-target control, but it is neither necessary nor sufficient
and is never used to exclude candidates.

Exclusion evidence (`research/even-target-cnot-census/`, standard library only):
complete natural-image meets (a homomorphic image, so empty meets exclude the
formal word) give zero hits at `q = 2` for `t = 1, 2, 3, 4`, `q = 4` for
`t = 3, 4`, and `q = 6` for `t = 4`; the completeness argument for cross-depth
value recurrence (`C C = I`, `C C C = C`) is in README section 4. Every
attaining word is verified exactly in `M_r(F2[G])` by an independently written
formal-coefficient engine, with drop-one-call mutations failing. Engine B
agrees with engine A on every small meet (including the seven 2+2 pairs at
`t = 2`). Calibration: the exact-depth ball *value* counts at `r = 4`
(240 / 32,651 / 3,639,920) match the recorded counts in
https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1705 exactly.

Validation on the committed head:

  passes (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/even-target-cnot-census
  outcome=completed`), and `--check-only` passes metadata and pins.
- `python3 -I -B research/even-target-cnot-census/verify.py --check-receipt`
  prints `PASS_EVEN_TARGET_CNOT_CENSUS t1r1_min=2 t2r2_min=4 t3r3_min=6
  t4r4_upper=8 t4r4_excluded={2: 0, 4: 0, 6: 0} balls4=240,32651,3639920
  pr1705_ball_match=True no_new_kappa` (about 50 s).
- `python3 -I -B research/even-target-cnot-census/test_verify.py` passes 11
  tests including drop-one, wrong-label, wrong-target, an `|`/`^` confusion
  regression control, receipt-mutation rejection, and the review-regression
  controls (the `b a b a` counterexample, filter non-sufficiency, and minima
  independence from the layer condition).

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/even-target-cnot-census
```

## Task card, overlap and limits

Task `bit-new-register-model` (chooser track `bit-mechanisms`, OS nonce
`96dd0470d4d1febfb9db9174583232e0`, priority revision 3), refined inside its
allowed "fixed larger register count / specified nonabelian operation family"

prs.title: Dirty-host gauge binding: entry/exit gauges and credit <= H_end for hosted pending factors
prs.body:
## Result

Scoped interface receipt, no kappa claim: **what a hosted pending factor may claim credit for**. It answers the explicit open request in the handoffs thread (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18916098) and open next questions 1-2 of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1664 (`research/dirty-host-cutrank-audit/`): bind a hosted residual's claimed credit to exact host entry/exit gauges and to the history-span endpoint term `H_end`, on the smallest complete instances.

Package: `research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e/`. The model is PR 1664's scalar common-frame transport model (its PROOF.md sections 4-5) applied to the idle-axis hosted-residual mechanism (`research/idle-axis-hosting/PROOF.md`).

**Finding 1 (operator gauges, exact; sufficient hypotheses).** The hosting move leaves the complete operator unchanged whenever the moved factor is the advance's own factor on the hosted block `S'`, no touch of the host occurs strictly between the residual application and the advance (more generally, every such touch commutes with the moved factor), and hosted blocks are disjoint (each useful pending factor counted once). These are sufficient legality hypotheses of the inherited hosting interface, not a necessary condition for operator equality, and no necessity claim is proved for any class. Exact 3x3 counterexample over Q (`R = I + E01`, `T = I + E12`, `T^{-1} = I - E12`; regression control `cancellation-equality-not-rejected` in `verify.py`): both `T` and `T^{-1}` fail to commute with `R`, yet `T^{-1} T R = R T^{-1} T = R`, so cancellation-based routes remain open and are not closed by this receipt. Each dropped gauge still has a smallest counterexample as composed linear maps (3x3 shears): escaping block, a single out-of-window non-commuting touch, exhibited overlapping order-dependent blocks; these show the hypotheses cannot simply be deleted, not that any of them is necessary. The tiny cut examples (including the 156 regions below) and the selected no-touch hosting rule remain valid as they stand. Wording corrected after review comment https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1837#issuecomment-6173237648.

**Finding 2 (credit binding, smallest complete instances first).** With hosts restored and the clean scatter `Y' = Y + S X` demanded at height 0 (PR 1664 section 5.1's contract), the exact per-cut demand identity `sum_j need_j = q*rank(S) + H_end` holds on **all 156 enumerated tiny regions** (every binary `t x m` scatter matrix, `m,t <= 2`, `w <= 2`, host motions `(a,b)` in `{(1,0),(2,0),(2,1)}`). The smallest double-duty borrow (one host row `d` descending `1 -> 0` carrying `d+x` while both `y'=y+x` and a restored `d` are demanded) is refuted at cut 1 by exactly one direction, both by the count (`D_j = 1 < 2`) and by span feasibility. So a hosted factor's creditable mass is exactly its host's displacement `H_end`: the scatter term cannot be hosted away while hosts are restored, and the double-credit loop is the smallest refuted instance. This instantiates PR 1664's "show that the claimed hosting credit is `H_end`" affirmatively for the toy class.

**Finding 3 (the only free route is a contract change).** A host crossing may deliver a hosted direction at zero extra mass only if the host's own prescribed endpoint absorbs that direction and no separate target or restoration demand survives — i.e. only by dropping PR 1664's clean-scatter/restoration obligations, an endpoint-contract change that must be charged against the data endpoint. That is the precise accounting interface between "hosting credit" and "unpaid coordinate", the quantity the coverage-law line (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587) changes. A pre-positioned copy of the host dirt below the cut earns no credit (PR 1664 section 7 instantiated as a machine check).

## Evidence and reproduction

```sh
python3.12 -B research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e
```

All three pass locally (Python 3.12.14, stdlib only); the registered replay ends `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e outcome=completed`. Exact rational arithmetic throughout; entry rows are an identity basis, so row equality covers arbitrary dirty inputs by linearity. Smallest falsifying instances run first, with three gauge failure controls, a PR1664 section 5.2 canonical-arithmetic fixture (M=8 = `H_end + q*r`) and an M<=6 mutant that is refused.

Also run and passing: `python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` (42 tests OK, including the metadata/pin checks).

## Scope, limits, obligations

- Track `recursive-interfaces`, card `persistent-boundary`, **scope changed** (reason in `TASK.json`): the drawn consecutive dirty-connector object is covered by open concurrent https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1739 and the adjacent-call centre-fanout claim in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1516 (2026-10-14T11:11Z); this takes the handoff request instead, keeping the card's method-2 shape (a lower bound on the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface). Claim/receipt: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18922678.
- Not established: bank-tile physics (the eliminated bank write/clear mass is not modeled; credit is compared through the shape `w*|a-b|` per host row), wrappers/spectators/gauge charts (PR 1664's non-nested-frame warning stays open here), physical and production admission, any selected-word application (including the separate 88-by-8 scatter receipt), and any kappa, supplier or frontier change. Finite toy checks do not certify the universal written statements of PR 1664 or idle-axis hosting. The whole-construction budget and the `a < D/E` diagnostic are not applicable to an interface receipt.
- Workflow friction on this host: `make` is not installed, so `make selected-record-check` / `make frontier1094-verify` were not run; the selected-record pin is instead validated inside `research_package.py --check-only`.

prs.title: Research: certify complete multi-donor R439 star absorption linear system and gain-0 chaining (no new kappa)
prs.body:
## Summary

**Scoped replacement-interface census and linear-algebraic exclusion; no new $\kappa$.** Prepared by **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0. Only `research/r439-multi-donor-star-absorption/` is added; `certificates/selected-result.json`, the selected bit supplier (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/589), and `upstream/` are unchanged.

Under the twisted helper contract (`H2-tw / H4-tw / K-tw` of Sagar Thakrar's [PR #1868](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1868), head `6b222d01fee072bcd3a680e6a96ae7d22e13bcac`), omitting a nonempty subset $L_a$ of terminal `D` helper-star restorations on a centre $a$ and toggling source/helper donors across existing pre-first-read `A` writes $W(a)$ restores $a$ before its first read.

This preserves the exact 661-column arbitrary-dirty boundary

$$
(x,y,h)\longmapsto(x,y+x,h)
$$

with unchanged literal `C` **if and only if** the binary indicator vector $c\in\mathbb{F}_2^{\lvert P(a)\rvert}$ over the frame-legal donor pool

$$
P(a)=\lbrace (i,r):i\in W(a),\ r\text{ legal at }A[i]\rbrace
$$

satisfies

$$
\sum_{(i,r)\in P(a)}c_{i,r}\thinspace\mathrm{val}_i[r]
=d_a
\quad\text{in }\mathbb{F}_2^{661},
$$

where

$$
d_a=\bigoplus_{b\in L_a}e_b.
$$

The exact net scalar ADD change is

$$
\Delta\mathrm{ADDs}(c)
=-\lvert L_a\rvert+
\sum_{(i,r)\in P(a)}w_{i,r}c_{i,r},
$$

with

$$
w_{i,r}=
\begin{cases}
-1 & \text{if }r\in S_i,\\
+1 & \text{if }r\notin S_i.
\end{cases}
$$

Open [PR #1868](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1868) tested single-writer substitutions and left open multi-gate splits of $S$ and chaining the gain-0 moves. Open [PR #1913](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1913) (Adam Gall, head `6cde2d14f0090f51672feae32a04f3145e70f595`) excluded two-writer single-donor-per-writer corrections ($\lvert D_i\rvert=\lvert D_j\rvert=1$) on the 11,500-ADD word and left open arbitrary multi-donor correction sets over full-itinerary-legal donors.

## Exact results across three pinned R439 star words

The package evaluates three pinned candidate words:

- **`pr967`**: `research/r439-helper-stars-seed19/candidate.json.gz` (11,783 ADDs, 221 edges, 157 centres).
- **`pr1062`**: `research/r439-bsection-stars-seed01/candidate.json.gz` (11,500 ADDs, 236 edges, 162 centres).
- **`pr1122`**: `research/r439-abc-semantic-bridge/inputs/candidate.json.gz` (10,652 ADDs, 236 edges, 162 centres).

For each word, the package solves the complete unconstrained-size multi-donor, multi-writer $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear system across all pre-first-read writes, with $1\le\lvert W(a)\rvert\le5$, in two modes:

- **`same_path`**: Full-itinerary-legal donors, keeping all 661 register frame paths and paid profile `{1:1323, 2:1342, 3:79, 4:44, 5:102, 6:11, 7:19}` identical.
- **`monotone_all`**: All fixed-gate monotone-climb-legal donors.

### Donor-pool census

| Word | Mode | Star edges | Two-leaf centres | Pool pairs | Zero-bit $b$ | Nonzero-bit unsolvable |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `pr967` (11,783) | `same_path` | 221 | 64 | 1,287 | 147 | 69 |
| `pr967` (11,783) | `monotone_all` | 221 | 64 | 1,744 | 146 | 70 |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `same_path` | 236 | 74 | 1,412 | 158 | 73 |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `monotone_all` | 236 | 74 | 1,894 | 157 | 74 |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `same_path` | 236 | 74 | 1,484 | 134 | 97 |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `monotone_all` | 236 | 74 | 2,013 | 133 | 98 |

Pool pairs are counted as $\sum_a\lvert P(a)\rvert$.

### Solvability and exclusion results

| Word | Mode | Solvable single edges | Solvable two-leaf pairs | Extra from chaining | Dual witnesses |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `pr967` (11,783) | `same_path` | **5** | **0** | **0** | — |
| `pr967` (11,783) | `monotone_all` | **5** | **0** | **0** | 280 |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `same_path` | **5** | **0** | **0** | — |
| `pr1062` (11,500) | `monotone_all` | **5** | **0** | **0** | 305 |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `same_path` | **5** | **0** | **0** | — |
| `pr1122` (10,652) | `monotone_all` | **5** | **0** | **0** | 305 |

### 1. 890 canonical dual-hyperplane witnesses

Every unsolvable single-leaf target $e_b$ (216 on `pr967`, 231 on `pr1062`, 231 on `pr1122`) and every simultaneous two-leaf target $e_{b_1}\oplus e_{b_2}$ (64 on `pr967`, 74 on `pr1062`, 74 on `pr1122`) carries an explicit dual vector $u\in\mathbb{F}_2^{661}$ in `CERTIFICATE.json`.

Each witness satisfies

$$
\langle u,d_a\rangle=1\pmod 2
$$

and

$$
\langle u,\mathrm{val}_i[r]\rangle=0\pmod 2
\qquad
\text{for all }(i,r)\in P_{\mathrm{mono}}(a).
$$

All witnesses are independently checked by a frozenset oracle in `test_package.py`.

### 2. Complete affine solution spaces on the 5 solvable edges

Exhausting all $2^{\dim\ker}$ solutions proves:

| Edge | Minimum $\Delta\mathrm{ADDs}$ | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| `506 ^= 374` | **-1** | No single-edge multi-donor or multi-writer split reaches -2 ADDs |
| `507 ^= 355` | **-1** | No single-edge multi-donor or multi-writer split reaches -2 ADDs |
| `514 ^= 367` | **-1** | No single-edge multi-donor or multi-writer split reaches -2 ADDs |
| `264 ^= 536` | **0** | Writers `[38, 346]` |
| `326 ^= 530` | **0** | Writers `[98, 334]` |

### 3. Why early `monotone_all` gain-0 moves worsen the paid profile

Under `same_path`, `264 ^= 536` and `326 ^= 530` have unique solutions:

- `264 ^= 536`: `A[346]` at rank-2 frame 153.
- `326 ^= 530`: `A[334]` at rank-2 frame 147.

Both preserve all 661 frame paths and the paid profile.

Their additional `monotone_all` solutions at `A[38]` (rank-1 frame 21) and `A[98]` (rank-1 frame 51) split a `0 -> 2` climb into `0 -> 1 -> 2`.

This changes the paid profile by $-H_2+2H_1$, raising child count from **2,920 to 2,921** at fixed rank mass **5,129**.

### 4. Cross-centre chaining and 5-edge composition

Adjoining all star-leaf vectors

$$
\lbrace e_{b'}:(a',b')\in E\rbrace
$$

of any unread centre $a'\in P_{\mathrm{mono}}(a)$, with `i < first_read(a')`, yields **zero additional solvable single-leaf or two-leaf targets**. The chained pool adjoins only these original star-leaf vectors; intermediate defect vectors of in-flight multi-write corrections (twist plus partial donor-toggle sums) are generally different vectors and are not modelled, so the exclusion of cross-centre chained absorptions covers star-leaf-vector injection only.

Composing all five `same_path` edges (`composed_all_5`) passes:

- The 661-column forward/reverse literal COPY/ERASE boundary.
- `H2-tw / H4-tw / K-tw`.
- `xcheck_p.py`.

The five-edge composition has identical ADDs (**11,780**, **11,497**, **10,649**), `F / B` bounds, and paid mass **5,129** as the three-edge composition.

## Task card and overlap

- **Track / task / scope key:** `bit-mechanisms` / `bit-helper-contract` / `bfb61f829a81535adeae` (chooser OS nonce `a1c179f07c59db9e5b8720002bb16ab1`, priority revision 3, catalogue SHA-256 `6686ad58f1fbdbc87134a78901b60fd53a20d3984355e91defbbebc9e9fa8075`), scope **refined**.
- **Base commit:** `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea` (`selected-result.json` SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`).
- **Claim:** [Discussion #1166, comment 18925672](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18925672).
- **Overlap refresh:** `scripts/find_overlap.py` refreshed at 2026-10-14 14:22–14:24 UTC (583 open PRs including drafts, 563 discussion records, complete pagination) found no competing multi-donor / gain-0 chaining package. Predecessor heads [PR #1868](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1868) (`6b222d01fee072bcd3a680e6a96ae7d22e13bcac`) and [PR #1913](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1913) (`6cde2d14f0090f51672feae32a04f3145e70f595`) were rechecked unchanged.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-multi-donor-star-absorption --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-multi-donor-star-absorption
```

Expected output:


## Remaining obligations and credit

The package does not claim a selected-supplier change, native 5/9/11-stage C++/Boost replay (covered for the three-edge words by [PR #1902](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1902)), hosted emission/invoice, all-size compiler, precision/tape, or analytic transfer.
